interaction: reactor pressure loop vs reboiler level loop: different units, no shared loop or alarm

judge.reason: Proposal would further close the PCV (lowering setpoint reduces opening). To relieve high reactor pressure due to PCV degradation, the PCV should be opened more, i.e., increase R_PIC setpoint within its bounds.

Addresses H2 PCV capacity degradation by biasing PCV opening toward more capacity with a small, reversible increase in R_PIC (3.0→3.2 bar) within bounds. Likely reduces backpressure and lowers reactor pressure without approaching SIF/alarm limits. Changes only PCV loop; no other variables adjusted.
Bottoms pump primary failed with a healthy standby; START_SPARE on BOTTOMS directly addresses the diagnosed pump_trip without affecting other controls.

Actions address the fault: start spare bottom pump due to primary failure; modest R_PIC setpoint increase to relieve reactor pressure from PCV capacity degradation. Throughput unchanged. No action pushes variables toward SIF limits.

Proposal incorrectly sets R_PIC to 3.2 bar (lower than current 3.3) which would reduce PCV opening, counterproductive for PCV capacity degradation. Also starting the spare bottoms pump is appropriate, but the R_PIC adjustment direction is wrong and risks not addressing the fault.
Addresses H2 PCV capacity degradation by nudging PCV authority (R_PIC) within limits and swapping to healthy Bottoms pump. Changes are targeted and within SIF/alarm bounds; minimizes disturbance.

Proposal starts a healthy spare pump to restore bottom flow without altering setpoints, addressing the h2_pcv_stuck_closed fault symptom indirectly by stabilizing CSTR outflow and reactor pressure without risking SIF limits.

Proposal does not address the diagnosed fault (H2 PCV stuck-closed). Starting the BOTTOMS spare pump and reducing throughput do not influence the PCV actuator fault; they may relieve some downstream loading but do not resolve the PCV command-actual mismatch or relieve reactor pressure via venting. This risks driving toward SIF limits if pressure remains high. The smallest, appropriate action would focus on the PCV loop or vent strategy (e.g., isolating the PCV fault, switching PCV control to a safe mode or safe vent path if available, or commanding a bumpless transfer to manual with safe, test

Addresses fault by providing an alternate vent path (H2_BDV) to relieve reactor pressure when PCV is stuck; also maintains bottoming flow via spare pump, which is reasonable given pump-train reliability concerns. However, START_SPARE for BOTTOMS is arguably unnecessary since the spare is already configured as active; this introduces an extra, non-essential change.

The proposed change targets the diagnosed fault (PCV stuck closed) by relieving reactor holdup via R_LIC and modestly reducing feed throughput, avoiding R_PIC (saturated) and staying within setpoint bounds. It minimizes disturbance and avoids pushing loops toward SIF/plant-trip limits.

Targets the diagnosed fault (H2 PCV stuck closed) with the smallest, reversible adjustments that relieve load without engaging R_PIC. Actions stay within regulator/tank limits and avoid pushing toward SIF/trip limits.
Addresses the fault by switching to a healthy spare bottom-pump to restore discharge path and relieve load without moving other controls; minimal change and avoids driving loops toward SIF limits.

The proposed actions target reducing CSTR holdup and downstream pressure by lowering feed throughput and by nudging the level controller setpoint to drive higher outflow, which can help offset the stuck PCV condition. Changes are within bounds (R_LIC SP 25–68 kmol; throughput target 60–70 kmol/h is within typical operating envelope) and avoid forcing the saturated R_PIC loop. The plan minimizes disturbance while addressing the fault symptoms (PCV command-actual mismatch and reactor pressure concern) and keeps operations within SIF/alarm limits.

Plan2 changes (increase R_LIC to 65) push cstr_holdup toward R_L_HH limit (62 kmol) and risks tripping alarms/SIFs; it also counteracts the intended load-relief from lowered throughput. It does not isolate the root fault (H2 PCV stuck closed) and adds unnecessary disturbance.
Reduces CSTR holdup/pressure by lowering feed load without touching saturated R_PIC or triggering SIFs; aligns with fault relief and minimal-change principle.

R_LIC setpoint change to 58 kmol may push reactor holdup upward when pv is below setpoint, counteracting load relief. Throughput reduction to 50 kmol/h is reasonable and small, but the R_LIC setpoint should not be lowered in this episode.
Addresses the h2_pcv_stuck_closed fault by reducing feed load to lower reactor holdup and pressure without changing regulator setpoints. Within SIF/alarm envelopes; minimal intervention.

Proposal targets R_PIC_out_of_range by unloading the CSTR/column feed (increase R_LIC to reduce holdup and pressure) and modestly reducing throughput to ease overall load. Setpoints stay within SIF/alarm limits (R_LIC setpoint 60 kmol, below R_L_HH 68 kmol). No direct adjustment of R_PIC (saturated) or other unrelated variables.

Action directly targets R_PIC_out_of_range by reducing plant load (throughput) rather than tweaking saturated loops. It avoids moving saturated loops (R_PIC, RB_LIC) setpoints and keeps within SIF/alarm margins (cstr_pressure ~1.12 bar, well below R_P_HH). Throughput reduction is the smallest step toward relief of cstr pressure/holdup pressure interactions while preserving safety. Since RB_LIC and R_PIC are saturated, decreasing throughput relieves load without provoking other limits.

Fault is R_PIC_out_of_range with saturated loop; reducing throughput is the smallest healthy lever to relieve overall plant load without moving a saturated loop. Throughput reduction from 40 to 35 kmol/h will lower reactor pressure/holdup and bring conditions toward limits, while avoiding SIF/trip thresholds.

Proposal uses a large throughput reduction (35 to 30 kmol/h) to relieve R_PIC saturation. Throughput change should be the minimal adjustment to bring PV back within limits, not a large step. Also no explicit preference for using standby pumps when available; if RB_LIC or other pumps are healthy, consider load relief via smaller throughput decrease or incremental pump-load redistribution first.
Fault is R_PIC_out_of_range with saturated R_PIC; reducing throughput by a small amount relieves load without driving R_PIC toward its limit or altering other SIFs.

Proposed actions target the root cause (R_PIC out of range due to elevated CSTR pressure/holdup) by reducing plant load (throughput) and easing reboiler holdup via RB_LIC setpoint. This avoids pushing the already saturated R_PIC and RB_LIC loops while aiming to bring the PVs back toward setpoints. Changes stay within alarm/SIF limits and use the smallest practical lever combination to restore normal operation.
Reduces throughput to relieve saturated R_PIC and DR_LIC, addressing R_PIC_out_of_range with a small, reversible change within bounds.

The fault is primarily R_PIC_out_of_range (saturated) with DR_LIC also saturated. The plan aims to relieve DR_LIC load by lowering its setpoint to the minimum (16.0) to reduce distillate demand and help bring the system back toward setpoints without aggravating the saturated loop. This is the smallest, targeted action addressing DR_LIC saturation while leaving other loops unchanged. However, the root cause (R_PIC saturation) remains and should be monitored; ensure no secondary limits are violated and consider using a standby pump if permissible within the fault scenario.

Action_relieves R_PIC load by reducing plant throughput; keeps R_PIC itself unchanged and within bounds; small, reversible change aimed at returning holdup/pressure toward normal without touching SIF limits.

Fault-targeted: reduces CSTR holdup and downstream load to relieve saturated R_PIC without stressing SIFs; uses smallest, reversible adjustments (R_LIC and throughput) and avoids touching R_PIC directly.

Addresses diagnosed fault (R_PIC_out_of_range) by relieving load on the saturated R_PIC loop through lowering R_LIC to reduce CSTR holdup and downstream pressure/flow requirements. The change remains within bounds (25–68 kmol) and does not push toward SIF limits; it targets the symptom with a minimal, reversible adjustment.

Fault addressed by relieving reactor pressure loop saturation (R_PIC) via load relief on CSTR (increase R_LIC outflow) and reduce feed (throughput). Changes stay within alarm/SIF limits and avoid touching saturated R_PIC or DR_LIC. Proportional adjustments target holdup reduction with minimal necessary moves.
